narrative: OMX30 faces mixed signals this morning. While the index sits +2.5% above its 200-day MA (bullish macro backdrop), technical deterioration is evident: MACD below signal, RSI at neutral 42.8, and critically an ADX of 13.3 indicating weak trend conviction with bearish directional bias. Global correlation is negative at -61.1bps—DAX and Asia weakness, coupled with a 4.5% oil surge on Hormuz disruption concerns, will pressure industrials and consumer discretionary. However, rising yields (+15bp US 10Y to 5.277%) provide support for banks via wider NIM, while defensive names like AstraZeneca and Essity benefit from risk-off rotation. The stochastic K/D at 11.9/20.2 (oversold) presents mean reversion opportunity if we stabilise. Watch whether USD/SEK's modest strength (+0.10%) can buoy exporters (Atlas Copco, Volvo, Ericsson).
morningBrief: OMX30 likely to open soft, tracking DAX weakness and Asian selloff. Oil's 4.5% jump will weigh on Volvo, Atlas Copco and SSAB (industrials/materials cost concern), while banks (SEB, Handelsbanken) get bid from 15bp yield rise. Defensives (AstraZeneca, Essity) in favour as risk-off mood persists; copper +0.75% supports Boliden as bright spot. Technical picture weak: MACD below signal, ADX 13.3 (no trend), stochastic oversold at 11.9—confidence capped at Low due to ADX <18. Key support 3085 (lower Bollinger), resistance 3180 (50-MA). USD/SEK +0.10% provides minor tailwind for exporters but insufficient to offset oil headwind. Watch US Jobless Claims 14:30 CET for late-session reprieve or fresh pressure.
